enrichment.headline: Approves $67,260,334.53 in payroll payments for July through September 2021
enrichment.summary: The board is approving the district's payroll payments for the first three months of the fiscal year: 3,021 printed paychecks and 24,009 direct deposits. The total is $67,260,334.53, from July 1, 2021 through September 30, 2021.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Payroll Warrants and Direct Deposits— Fiscal Year 2021-2022 - July 1, 2021 - September 30, 2021 - Chief Business Officer

enrichment.headline: Approves $64,800,465.68 in vendor payments for July through September 2021
enrichment.summary: The board is approving the bills the district paid to vendors in the first three months of the 2021-2022 fiscal year. This covers 1651 printed checks totaling $64,800,465.68, from July 1, 2021 through September 30, 2021.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Accounts Payable Warrants - Fiscal Year 2021-2022 – July 1, 2021 - September 30, 2021 - Chief Business Officer

enrichment.headline: Pays Jensen Hughes up to $101,700 to design a new fire alarm system at Hintil Kuu Child Development Center
enrichment.summary: Jensen Hughes, an engineering firm in Concord, would design a replacement for the existing fire alarm systems at the Hintil Kuu Child Development Center, including site visits and surveys. The agreement is for up to $101,700, which includes a $5,000 contingency fee. Work is scheduled from November 4, 2021 to June 29, 2024.

items.group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Adds $37,628.20 to Viatron's records contract for the Cole Administration Center project
enrichment.summary: This amendment adds services for Viatron Systems: listing all the files it retrieved from the district's storage space, building a new database log of them, and organizing them alphabetically. It adds $37,628.20 and raises the contract limit from $308,795.00 to $346,423.20. All other terms stay the same.

items.group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Confirms a partnership with Oakland REACH for programming at Sojourner Truth Independent Study School
enrichment.summary: The board is ratifying (confirming) a memorandum of understanding with Oakland REACH. It sets out what each side will do for REACH programming and partnership at Sojourner Truth Independent Study School from July 21, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The text states no dollar amount.

pulled.summary: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

enrichment.headline: Ratifies a contract paying a contractor up to $32,400 to support drug and health education in classrooms
enrichment.summary: The district is ratifying (confirming) an agreement for 1,080 hours of work supporting teachers, in both online and in-person classrooms, on lessons about drug education, holistic health, and how race, law and politics affect rates of incarceration and exploitation of youth. It runs September 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 for up to $32,400.

enrichment.summary: Children Rising, an Oakland organization, would tutor 2nd and 3rd graders in reading and math at MLK and Lafayette Elementary Schools. The district is ratifying (confirming) the agreement for August 9, 2021 through May 25, 2022, for up to $8,325.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Hires Family Engagement Lab for up to $200,000 of text messaging to families, without bidding
enrichment.summary: Family Engagement Lab of San Francisco would provide text messaging services between schools and parents or caregivers from August 2, 2021 through June 30, 2022, for up to $200,000. The board is using a sole source exception, which skips public bidding, and adopting a resolution to allow it.

enrichment.headline: Hires Oakland Public Education Fund for up to $250,000 of COVID-19 contact tracing, without bidding
enrichment.summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund would carry out COVID-19 contact tracing and related activities from August 15, 2021 through June 30, 2022, for up to $250,000. The board is using a sole source exception, which skips public bidding, and adopting a resolution to allow it.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for School Services of California to represent OUSD at the state Capitol
enrichment.summary: School Services of California, based in Sacramento, would develop strategies, monitor legislation and budget items affecting the district, and lobby the Legislature and State Administration. The district is ratifying (confirming) the agreement for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, for up to $50,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - School Services of California - Office of the Chief of Staff

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for a contractor to write and manage grants for the Chief of Staff's office
enrichment.summary: A contractor in Oakland would write grant proposals and reports, edit and research them, and coordinate the grant submission process for the Office of the Chief of Staff. The district is ratifying (confirming) the agreement for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, for up to $50,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Records the law firm's name change to Davis, Bengtson & Young, with no added cost
enrichment.summary: This amendment to the district's memorandum of understanding and engagement policy with its law firm only changes the firm's name from Davis and Young to Davis, Bengtson & Young, effective July 29, 2021. No money or time is added, and all other terms stay the same.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

schools: Coliseum Prep Academy at Havenscourt High School
